summary: TerraTwin is an interactive planetary scouting application that compares orbital measurements from the Moon and Mars against live Earth satellite telemetry. It identifies new, under-studied terrestrial analog sites, scores them across NASA's four core criteria (Topography, Geology, Environment, and Resources), and generates field-ready characterization dossiers for mission planners.
details: TerraTwin is an advanced planetary analog and solar flux workstation designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to bridge the gap between orbital data and terrestrial field testing by cross-referencing eight verified lunar and Martian targets against sixteen inland Earth analog sites. Developed using Python, JavaScript, Three.js (globe.gl), and Leaflet.js, the workstation solves critical geographic and data fragmentation challenges through a deterministic 4-pillar similarity engine that scores terrestrial locations across topography, geology, environment, and resources. It features an interactive 3D WebGL globe with hover-only site labels and pulsing radar beacons, live telemetry scanning via NASA POWER and Copernicus DEMs, a 12-month seasonal time-travel simulator, an interactive solar array surface area calculator (\text{m}^2), and a rover slope-traverse physics simulator. By streamlining analog site selection for NASA's Artemis program and future outposts while embedding protected land stewardship protocols and multi-agency open data archives, TerraTwin significantly accelerates mission planning, de-risks multi-million-dollar hardware like cryogenic permafrost drills, and optimizes field campaigns for planetary exploration.
